I found a valid allocation that spills nodes 0, 4 and 22, for a total spill cost of 3 + 2 + 3 = 8. I did not prove this is the minimum, so a cheaper solution may exist.

**Approach:**
1. I started by spilling the cheap, high-degree nodes 0, 6, 12, 25 and 28.
2. I then colored greedily around the K4 on nodes 10, 11, 13 and 16. Coloring that clique forces the colors of nodes 3, 7, 14 and 18.
3. Node 22 (cost 3) then had all four colors among its neighbors, so I spilled it.
4. Node 4 (cost 3) was blocked the same way, because 3, 11, 16 and 18 use all four colors, so I spilled it too.
5. Finally I added back every spilled node that could be recolored in. Nodes 12, 6 and 25 fit directly. Node 28 fit after I recolored node 5 from 1 to 2. Node 0 could not be added back.

I checked every edge of the final coloring against the edge list and found no conflicts.
